tweetMedia.transcription: Some breaking news now just coming out of Israel where it's being reported that rockets have fallen in several areas in the center of the country. Let's go straight over to Noor Arde. She joins us from Ramallah in the occupied West Bank. And Noor, what are we hearing about the impact of those fallen rockets? Well, we're not hearing, Sami, because the military censor in Israel has not cleared information for publication yet. What we can tell you, though, is that eyewitnesses are talking about plumes of smoke. They're talking about several areas of impact. Now, the areas that have been targeted, we keep telling our viewers the center of Israel. Let's explain what does that mean. It means that the area that is being targeted is where about 44% of the Israeli population lives. This is where the Ben-Gurion Airport is. It is where several air bases and military bases are, the Ministry of Defense, the Mossad, our headquarters. This is a very strategic area for Israel. Targeting that area keeping all those millions of people in the shelters is extremely disruptive And this is what we heard for example from the mayor of Haifa saying that he will not ease restrictions that he will not allow schools to come back to resume activity because it was simply too risky. The alarms and the sirens are going off almost nonstop in Haifa and northern communities from rocket fire coming from Lebanon. And this is something that Israelis are increasingly frustrated with. There is no early warning to them. They have very few seconds, no more than a minute to get to the shelter. They cannot possibly think about and plan about going to work, sending kids to school, picking them up from school and so on. But throughout this war, Sami, we have to say I've never seen anything like it. The military censor has been adamant. It has imposed basically a blackout on where these missiles and rockets are falling, how many have been fired at Israel from Iran or Hezbollah, the information being tightly controlled. In fact, even having authorities arrest journalists who were deemed to have said too much on the air.
